Supported languages: go, dart, python, rust, swift, typescript, kotlin. Python uses uv; Rust uses Cargo. Swift uses SwiftPM and requires a Swift 6+ toolchain. TypeScript uses npm and Node for tests and quality tools; Bun compiles standalone CLIs. Kotlin uses the committed Gradle wrapper for one root Kotlin/JVM project.

Go supports binary/library; Dart supports library; Python supports package; Rust supports binary/library/package. Default remains binary. Swift supports binary/library; package mode is excluded. TypeScript supports library verification and binary CLI builds; library builds emit no release assets and require includeArtifacts=false. Kotlin supports library verification and binary JVM CLI distributions; library releases require includeArtifacts=false.

Defaults to ["./..."]. Go uses package patterns; Rust uses all workspace members or explicit crate names for library/package builds. Swift uses all root build targets or exact target names. TypeScript accepts only ./... for one root tsconfig.json project. Kotlin accepts only ./... for one root Gradle JVM project.

Enable optional tests during library/package builds and Rust binary builds. Rust tests selected crates on the active compiler host before cross-building. Swift tests the whole root package before library/binary builds. TypeScript checks types and optionally runs npm/Node tests before library or CLI builds. Applies to both Kotlin build modes.

Go main package defaults to ./cmd/<repo>; Rust package manifest directory defaults to a dot. Rust chooses the sole binary or package.default-run. Swift names an executable product or infers the only one. TypeScript CLI builds require an explicit source entry point included in tsconfig.json; library builds reject this field. Kotlin rejects mainPackage; Gradle application.mainClass selects the CLI entry point.

Go/Rust target matrix using os-arch strings. Rust maps to GNU Linux and Apple Darwin and MSVC Windows triples. Package mode rejects target matrices and --target. Swift supports only the native macOS or GNU/Linux host on amd64/arm64. TypeScript CLI targets must match the native Bun macOS or GNU/Linux amd64/arm64 host. TypeScript library mode rejects targets and --target. Kotlin rejects targets and --target because JVM distributions are platform-independent.
Explicit CGO mode for Go builds. When true build sets `CGO_ENABLED=1`; when false build sets `CGO_ENABLED=0`.
